$comment: Table of contents for the documentation published at https://proxybrowser.ubaidbinwaris.com/docs. Each page is docs/site/<slug>.md; scripts/sync-docs.mjs copies them into the website at build time.

pages.title: Introduction
pages.seoTitle: Introduction: free QA for your web forms
pages.description: What Proxy QA Browser is: a free, open-source desktop app for testing your own web forms by location, on emulated devices and in real browsers.

pages.title: Install
pages.seoTitle: Install on Windows, Linux and macOS
pages.description: Download and run Proxy QA Browser on Windows 10 and 11 (portable EXE), Linux (AppImage) and macOS 12+ (DMG): first launch, moving and uninstalling.

pages.title: First run
pages.seoTitle: First run: setup wizard and proxy keys
pages.description: The first-run set-up wizard: bundled browsers, optional proxy keys stored in the encrypted vault, the Manage keys window and a tour of the main window.

pages.title: Launching browsers
pages.seoTitle: Launch QA browsers through a proxy
pages.description: Launch Chrome, Edge, Brave or a bundled engine for QA through a built-in proxy provider or directly, in a fresh profile, with the exit IP checked first.

pages.title: Proxy providers
pages.seoTitle: Use your own proxy plan for QA testing
pages.description: Bring your own plan from a supported proxy provider: logins, location targeting by provider and sticky or rotating sessions. Not affiliated with any provider.

pages.title: Locations and devices
pages.seoTitle: Verify exit-IP location; emulate devices
pages.description: Target a country or a US state, city or ZIP, check the exit IP's reported location before the window opens, and emulate phone, tablet and desktop presets.

pages.title: Browsers
pages.seoTitle: Bundled and installed browsers for QA
pages.description: Bundled Chromium, Firefox and WebKit plus installed Chrome, Edge, Brave and Opera: one-click installs, detection without starting them, and known limits.

pages.title: Site access tokens
pages.seoTitle: Allowlist QA traffic in your own WAF
pages.description: Send a secret header only to origins you list, so your own staging WAF or CAPTCHA can allow QA traffic and your form backend can tag it as test leads.

pages.title: Updates
pages.seoTitle: Signed updates, online or from USB
pages.description: How signed online and USB updates are verified with Ed25519 and SHA-256, the computer copy, the startup update check and updating on macOS.

pages.title: Scenarios and matrices
pages.seoTitle: Scenarios, CSV datasets and test matrices
pages.description: Record QA scenarios, import CSV datasets, run browser × device × location matrices, compare screenshots, schedule runs and export JSON, JUnit or HTML.

pages.title: Consent, accessibility and performance checks
pages.seoTitle: Automated accessibility and script checks
pages.description: Check consent disclosures and checkboxes, lead-certificate scripts (TrustedForm, Jornaya LeadiD), axe-core accessibility rules and performance budgets.

pages.title: Self-healing selectors
pages.seoTitle: Self-healing selectors and locators
pages.description: How self-healing selectors keep recorded tests running when an id or class changes: up to four fallback locators, flagged in results, warn or fail modes.

pages.title: CI runner
pages.seoTitle: CI runner for headless browser tests
pages.description: Run exported scenarios and suites headless in CI with the command-line runner, the Docker image or the GitHub Action, with JSON, JUnit and HTML reports.

pages.title: MCP server
pages.seoTitle: MCP server for browser QA testing
pages.description: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP client so an AI assistant can run geo- and device-aware QA checks, with navigation limited to origins you allow.

pages.title: Security and privacy
pages.seoTitle: Security and privacy: vault, no telemetry
pages.description: The AES-256-GCM credential vault and OS keychain, what is never logged, Electron hardening, every network connection the app makes and where data is stored.

pages.title: Settings reference
pages.seoTitle: Settings reference: defaults and limits
pages.description: Reference for every Proxy QA Browser setting: where it lives, its default and allowed range, QA automation policy limits and environment variables.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.seoTitle: Troubleshooting and error codes
pages.description: Fix common problems with installing, proxies and locations, browsers, sessions, the vault and QA automation, and look up what each error code means.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.seoTitle: FAQ: cost, privacy, proxies and browsers
pages.description: Answers to common questions about Proxy QA Browser: cost, responsible use, data and privacy, proxy plans, browsers, emulated devices, CI and AI assistants.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.seoTitle: Architecture: processes, IPC and data
pages.description: How Proxy QA Browser is built: the Electron process model and IPC contracts, source layout, start-up, a launch step by step, providers, data and security.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.seoTitle: Contributing: set up, test and open a PR
pages.description: Set up a development environment, run the tests, follow the code conventions and project scope, add a proxy provider and open a pull request.

pages.title: Building and releasing
pages.seoTitle: Build, sign and release the desktop app
pages.description: Build the Windows EXE, Linux AppImage and macOS DMG, sign update manifests with Ed25519, publish tagged releases through CI and deploy the website.
